title: Which Website Platforms US Cities and Counties Use (50,000+) | SignalFeed.dev
description: Website platforms of US cities and counties of 50,000+: CivicPlus, Granicus govAccess, Revize, WordPress, Drupal and more, identified for 392 cities and 382 counties from DNS and page markers.
h1: Which website platforms US cities and counties of 50,000+ use
body:
Which content management systems do large US local governments run their websites on? It matters for ADA Title II work: the platform decides how documents are uploaded and linked, what accessibility tooling exists, and who a city calls about it. Cities and counties of 50,000+ reach the rule's compliance date on April 26, 2027.

How we identified platforms

  • First from the site's public DNS records, which often point to the hosting platform (no visit to the site needed).
  • Otherwise from markers in the homepage itself (for example CivicPlus document-center paths), on sites whose robots.txt allows a visit.
  • Sites that block visits and don't reveal a platform in DNS stay unidentified, so platforms that show up mainly through page markers are likely undercounted. Treat the shares as indicative.
  • These are observations of public records and pages, not vendor-confirmed customer lists. We don't name or rank any city or county here.

Get the per-entity list

The custom territory list ($99) gives every city and county of 50,000+ in the states you choose, with its website platform, the agenda and document systems it links to, and its PDF backlog numbers. See also the city and county Backlog Index pages and K-12 district platforms.
